events.summary:
FFWRLX

The National Weather Service in Charleston has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Northern Meigs County in southeastern Ohio...
Southeastern Vinton County in southeastern Ohio...

* Until 1115 AM EDT.

* At 928 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated between 1.5 and 2 inches of
rain have fallen from thunderstorms earlier this morning. Even
though the heavy rainfall has since ended, flash flooding will
continue. Emergency Management reported State Route 733 is closed
due to flooding near Willis Hill, and State Route 143 at State
Route 7 is also closed due to flooding.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Emergency management reported.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Pomeroy, Rutland, Chester, Wilkesville, Harrisonville, Darwin,
Dexter, Dyesville, Carpenter and Salem Center.

events.summary:
...The National Weather Service in Chicago has issued a Flood Warning
for the following rivers in Indiana...Illinois...

Kankakee River at Shelby affecting Lake IN and Newton Counties.

Thorn Creek at Thornton affecting Cook County.

For the Kankakee River...including Shelby...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Kankakee River from Near I-65 and De Motte downstream to
IL/IN state line, including the Shelby gauge.

* WHEN...From this afternoon to Sunday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 10.5 feet, Water overflows low-lying river banks along
Bluegrass Road east of Sumava Resorts and along Westwood Drive and
Island Boulevard near Shelby. Water begins to be diverted through
the Blackberry Marsh Spillway to reduce flood impacts.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:45 AM CDT Friday the stage was 10.4 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage this
afternoon. It may fall below flood stage as soon as late Sunday
morning, although additional rainfall in the forecast may prolong
flooding impacts.
- Flood stage is 10.5 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flash flooding and debris flows caused by excessive rainfall
continue to be possible over the Aspen Acres burn scar.

* WHERE...The Aspen Acres Burn Scar.

* WHEN...From noon MDT today through this evening.

* IMPACTS...Heavy rainfall over the Aspen Acres burn scar is expected
up to and during the period of the watch. Residents near the Aspen
Acres burn scar should prepare for potential debris flow. Be sure
to stay up to date with information from local authorities. Heavy
rainfall could trigger flash flooding of low-lying areas, urbanized
street flooding, and debris flows in and near recent wildfire burn
scars.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- National Weather Service Meteorologists are forecasting
thunderstorms with heavy rainfall over the burn scar, which may
lead to flash flooding and debris flows.
- Some locations that may experience flash flooding include...
Beulah, San Isabel, and highways 165 and 78 in and around Aspen
Acres Burn Scar.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Indiana...

Driftwood River near Edinburgh.

.Recent periods of heavy rainfall have led to minor flooding along
the Driftwood River near Edinburgh. Flooding will persist over the
weekend into Monday morning.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Driftwood River near Edinburgh.

* WHEN...Until early Monday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 13.2 feet, Lowland flooding in progress along
Driftwood River in northern Bartholomew County on April 6, 2011.
Double Y Saddle Club area flooded. At least 6 inches of water
flowing over CR 950N to Club. Water is less than one foot away
from CR 330W just south of its intersection with Ohio Ridge Rd. CR
500N west of CR 250W is flooded blocking vehicular access to
residences near the river bank. Lowell Public Access site is open
but ramp is totally flooded. Water close to one residence at
Shelby CR 1000S and CR 900W.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 AM EDT Friday the stage was 11.1 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours
ending at 7:30 AM EDT Friday was 11.1 feet.
- Forecast...The river will fall below flood stage late this
morning to 10.9 feet this afternoon. It will then rise above
flood stage late this afternoon to 12.8 feet early tomorrow
afternoon. It will fall below flood stage again early Sunday
afternoon.
- Flood stage is 11.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
